title and abstract.summary: The study measured traditional community metrics (abundance, richness, Shannon diversity) and functional trait metrics (body length, wing morphology, activity time, phenology, and diet) for ground beetle communities across a restored grassland chronosequence over three years.

introduction.summary: The study examined the ground beetle community assembly in restored tallgrass prairie using a restoration succession chronosequence, describing beetles from both taxonomic- and trait-composition perspectives.

methods.summary: The study measured the presence of bison on various restored and remnant grassland sites within the Nachusa Grasslands preserve.

discussion.summary: The study measured the functional trait composition of the ground beetle community across different successional ages in new tallgrass prairie restorations, focusing on how functional richness and functional divergence changed over time.
